newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle were called steady to up 0.200 cent, livestock analysts said.
Carryover demand is expected in live cattle futures after cash cattle sold at firmer prices on Wednesday. Cash cattle actively traded at $65 per cwt, $1 higher than last week's sales.

But further weakness in boxed beef prices, despite expectations beef prices would bottom this week, and evening of positions ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report, will likely temper any gains, sources noted.
Wide placement estimates on the report have made for nervous trade at times in deferred contracts, they said.

July Placement estimates for the major seven states averaged 100.8 percent of a year ago and ranged from 96 to 106.5 percent. On-feed estimates averaged 115.6 and ranged between 114 to 117.8 percent and marketings averaged 105.5 percents and ranged from 103 to 107 percent of a year ago.

Feeder cattle were expected to show carryover demand following Wednesday's sharp turnaround. Further demand is expected to stem from the downturn in corn futures and lower indications in the CBOT corn pit Thursday monring, some analysts said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.20 at $81.19 per cwt.
